caption: The drawing depicts a detailed, lidded tankard with ornate decorations and two accompanying views: a top view of the handle and a small side elevation with measurements. The tankard is cylindrical with a broad base that slightly narrows towards the top, ending in a domed lid that has a finial for gripping. The lid extends slightly beyond the rim of the tankard. The body of the tankard is adorned with elaborate scrollwork, foliage, and two nude human figures, each standing on either side of a central oval medallion. Inside the medallion, two clothed persons, one holding a staff, are shown in a conversational pose. The lower border features a repeated leaf motif and a double-lined edge. To the left of the tankard, the handle is rendered in isolation, showing intricate decoration and the initials “WC IEEC” inscribed lengthwise. In the top right corner, a technical side view gives the tankard’s principal measurements: 6 1/2 inches in height and 5 3/4 inches in width, including a side profile of the handle and lid. The drawing is monotone, made with fine black or grey lines on a light beige background.
title: Silver Tankard
cluster: #19 — Ceramic Arts: Pottery, Stoneware, and Porcelain
